spans.text: Carriage F17, Intercontinental Railway train "Future".
Beep-beep-beep!!!!
The shrill blare of the alarm echoes throughout the crowded carriage, plunging the already noisy crowd further into chaos.
The entire carriage is illuminated by flashing red light, and the alarm only makes the passengers complain that much more.
...Miss Catherine, all I did was put my luggage on the rack...
Yup.
Catherine is being tossed about by the flow of the crowd, and she reaches out in an effort to free herself.
...Miss Catherine, why does our car not have any stewardess?
Huh. Ask the cops.
...Miss Catherine, this alarm has been going off nonstop all this time.
Miss Catherine...
After being pushed around by the crowd and being constantly nagged, Catherine can take it no longer and erupts with a shout.
Catherine's dead! Quit bothering me! God, you're such a pain in the ass!!!
Erma, all I did was buy you a ticket, I didn't agree to be your full-time babysitter!
The Doll called Erma isn't much better off than Catherine right now.
Her petite frame means she's been squashed up against the wall by the pressure of the milling crowd.
...I just wanted to know if I had caused the alarm to go off by stuffing my luggage onto the rack.
If that was the case, is there anything I can do to fix it? Will I need to pay a fine or something?
You're overthinking this! Don't bother paying it unless you're paying it to me!
Erma tries to ask another question, but there is a turn up ahead and she is almost tossed to the ground and trampled...
A pair of reliable arms extend from under her armpits—in the next moment, a tall figure is holding up little Erma while forcing them both away.
If the crowd is like a great man-eating beast, then she has been snatched from its jaws by a figure of steel that is methodically working its way free of all obstacles in its path.
...This place is too cramped. You should be careful.
...Thank you.
Miss Catherine... You should have told this girl what to expect on the train.
This is clearly her first time on an intercontinental train.
After lowering Erma to the ground, the scary-looking droid carefully puts his luggage down by his feet.
Humph, worry about yourself, Mis-ter-Pa-vel! Where does a tin can like you get off on lecturing me?
Also, you think you paid me a lot? That's just the ticket price. It doesn't include the service charge!
Pavel shakes his head and continues speaking to Erma in a patient tone.
...You can hang onto my shoulders, if you'd like. That would be more spacious.
Intercontinental train tickets are hard to get, and even a standing room ticket in a second-class carriage is quite a luxury for Dolls.
Pavel's voice is a little muffled, but he carefully shields the girl with his large frame and keeps the crush behind him away from her.
...Thank you, Mr. Pavel. My name is Erma.

Erma gingerly grabs Pavel's arm, then uses it as a handhold to propel herself up his back. Immediately, she gains a much better view of the area from her high perch—though it looks like she's dangling from his body.
It's not a very comfortable position, but at the very least she doesn't need to worry about being crushed in this sardine can of a carriage.
Hey—help me up too!
I can only carry so much weight.
Tsk, never mind then... Hey, Pavel, put your luggage on the rack behind you!
It's taking up so much space down here.
Catherine tries to stand on top of Pavel's suitcase, but he stops her.
Let me do it.
...The alarm is still going off. It's been doing that since I put my stuff on the luggage rack.
Don't worry, it's not your fault.
...We've entered the "unregulated area".
An unregulated area? What does that mean?
There is a Red Zone between Warsaw and Poznań, at the Soviet-German border.
Once we enter it, the radiation intensity spikes and it's easy for the carriage sensors to generate false positive alerts.
However, it's just an alert, and there are purification devices on the train, so it should be alright. Also, the police have all gotten off the train, so nobody will mind.
...I see.
Thank you for explaining all this to me.
It IS a little loud, though.
The volume is a bit too much for a child.
Are you really treating her like a human kid just because she looks short?
Snap.
Before Catherine can finish, Pavel rips the noisy alarm off the wall.
Startled by the shower of sparks, Catherine stares at Pavel with her eyes wide.
...You didn't need to destroy public property, right?
The police have all gotten off the train, so nobody will mind.
Pavel shrugs and repeats himself.
Besides, it really was loud.
The cops aren't around but the security cameras are!
God, I don't know what to say... When they ask you to pay for damages, we'll see—
Stomp.
Halfway through her griping, a passenger from behind Catherine steps on her foot.
OWWWWWW—Hey!! Quit pushing!
Ahhhh—!! I'm so pissed off, why do I have to be the one squeezing with people in the second-class carriage anyway?!
Catherine sighs and looks at her communicator—
Click. The call connects.

Perhaps it's because they've entered a Red Zone, or because reception in the second-class carriage is really bad, it has taken a very long time for Catherine to get the call through. The moment it connects, she starts complaining.
...Catherine?
Hey, Maggie! Why did you have to give me a second-class ticket?!

Because I was worried about you slacking off in the dining carriage again. Remember last time when you forgot to check the tickets and caused over a dozen of our clients to be unable to board the train?
...Oh come on, we agreed—no raking over the ashes!
Have you confirmed the identities of all the Dolls boarding the train for this trip?
Of course. They're squeezed up with me in Carriage 17... If I'd known, I wouldn't have put them all in 17. When you get tickets next time, make sure they're more evenly distributed.
It's best to keep them on a short leash to make sure they can all board the Colt Express.
This DOES concern our bodies for the rest of our lives, after all.
Aw, relax!
A loud voice suddenly cuts through the clamor of the carriage—
Dear passengers, may I have your attention please.
The Future is now in high-speed cruise mode.
Passengers who need to pay their outstanding ticket fares, please proceed to Carriage 9.
Dear passengers, may I have your attention please.
The Future is now in high-speed cruise mode.
Passengers who need to pay their outstanding ticket fares, please proceed to Carriage 9.
...Right, catch you later.
...Sure.
Catherine nods, and then hangs up her call with Maggie.
...It's time.
She struggles to her feet and leans against Pavel's large body.
Let's go. Everyone who wants to board the Colt Express, we should be heading out.
Our destination is Carriage F09.
...Got it.
...Let me lead the way.
Pavel pushes the crowd out of his way as he moves forward.
Despite how densely packed the passengers are, Pavel actually manages to strongarm a big enough gap for walking.
And so, the group slowly make their way toward Dining Carriage 9.
Soon, they have moved past the crowd and several carriages in between—
They are now just one door away from Carriage 9.
They are several minutes earlier compared to Catherine's earlier estimation.
...You're pretty good at this.
That performance would be enough to warrant a tip.
Not that I'd actually tip you, of course.
Just find a place to sit down once you go in.
Make sure you have your invitations with you. You'll automatically log onto the Colt Express when it's time.
An invitation?
...That's the Colt Express ticket I sold you!
Carriage F09, Intercontinental Railway train "Future".

The moment they enter, the gentle music flowing from the record player sets this place apart from the second-class carriages. Compared to the chaos back there, the atmosphere in the dining carriage is a vast improvement.
The passengers here are all elegant and refined, either enjoying their exquisite meals or clinking their wine glasses together.
Everyone looks easygoing and relaxed here, whether they're standing in the aisles, seated at the tables, or at the bar counter.
Catherine says nothing but heads straight to the counter. The others quickly find empty seats, leaving Erma alone to look around the carriage.
I really like this song, though its melody isn't very familiar to me.
We are honored by your praise. The truth is, we specially commissioned a renowned musician to create it just for us.
The stewardess calmly takes the passengers in stride as she serves them.
...The riesling here is very good. Can you send a bottle to my seat?
Of course. This wine is custom-brewed for the Future. Feel free to ask for more if you'd like.
I'll take three bottles, then.
Very well.
After looking around, Erma points to the dinner of one of the passengers and discreetly gets the attention of the stewardess.
Excuse me, I'd like what he's having, please.
...Sorry, but that set meal is for autumn only and we've already sold out.
...Do you have anything to drink, then?
...Go see for yourself at the bar.
Erma finds this distinct difference in treatment to be quite strange.
Meanwhile, Pavel has already found a table for two and is waving at her.
Since it's close to the bar counter, she goes over and sits down without a word.
...Am I very different from other people?
Hm, why do you say that?
It feels like the stewardess is treating me very differently from the others.
That's because you lack a certain scent.
Erma and Pavel turn to look at the speaker, who is a Doll bartender.
What kind of scent is that?
It's the smell of "money" that rich people have on them.
Huh?
Pffft, I was just kidding.
There aren't many passengers in the VIP and first-class carriages, so Susanna would have noted them all down. Therefore, anyone not on her list must be from the second-class carriages.
Does she need money that badly?
Well, this does affect the grade of our new bodies.
So yes, for Dolls, serving the right people really is very important.
...They're going to have a cocktail party here soon.
Do you have your invitations?
Erma and Pavel exchange glances, then they each take out a card that is roughly the size of a playing card.
The bartender nods.
Why don't you get yourselves a drink?
Someone usually pays for drinks around these times.
And besides, what comes next might take a while.
I am not equipped to process food and drink.
Then what will you have, miss?
...What would you pick if you were me?
...I'd go with a "Tequila Slammer".
We have a special version of it that's only available here. Since you've come all this way to board the train, it would be a waste not to try it.
...I'll have that, then.
The bartender Doll smiles and makes a note of their seat, then turns to the next passenger.
...Does the Colt Express refer to this particular carriage?
I don't think so. They say the Colt Express has been running for several years now, but nobody's ever seen what the manager looks like.
My guess is that he won't show himself to us.
Erma nods.
Have you noticed? It seems there are only Dolls left around here.
...Indeed. However, that's not strange either. After all, the Colt Express is a fairly new black market for Dolls.
Humans probably haven't taken part in it yet.
In that case... Why do you want to board the Colt Express, Mr. Pavel?
Pavel's headlamp, which is basically his eyes, flickers.
There's something... that I absolutely need to buy.
How about yourself?
There's something that I need to understand.
